text:
alex: Quick sync: pricing/packaging decision for 'Performance Lane' pilot. Two paths on the table: prepaid burst-packs (metered credits) vs. timeboxed SLA lanes (contracted short-term capacity). Need one clear direction for pilot deck.

toni: Sales feedback: customers prefer a simple, buy-and-use model. Bursts in discrete packs (e.g., 10k token-credits or 1k request-credits) map better to procurement. They hate surprise throttles.

cheng: Infra ops: we can implement softcaps + immediate throttle, or strict reservations that isolate a slice of capacity. Reservations are heavier ops and increase cost. Softcaps with preemption rules easier to roll out.

maya: Product take: recommend hybrid for pilot — reserved minimal baseline (to satisfy compliance) + short burst packs that push you into priority scheduling but still marked best-effort. Need clear UX: buy, allocate to route, expire.

alex: example customer ask: 2 routes, baseline 40 rps each, occasional 3m spikes to 180 rps. They want predictable behavior during spikes.

pricing-bot: Auto-scan: suggested surge multiplier missing. Recommend surge_price = 3x unit cost for on-demand top-ups. Logged ticket PR-712.

toni: Pricing nuance: are we selling 'credits' by concurrency-minutes or by requests? Sales favors requests because customers think in API calls. Engineering prefers concurrency-minutes (easier to enforce and bill for time in queue).

cheng: enforcement note: concurrency-minutes lets us cap by servers/slots. Implementation: one credit = one concurrent request for 60s. Requests shorter than 60s prorate down to 1s granularity. Billing engine needs small change.

maya: buyer kit ask: show three worked examples (web app burst, nightly batch, telemetry-heavy endpoint). Each should include cost calc, when throttle happens, and fallback UI text.

alex: contract/terms: legal-bot, can we include 'best-effort burst' language + a non-guarantee clause?

legal-bot: Suggested clause (summary): "Burst capacities are offered on a best-effort basis. Purchasing Burst Credits increases a customer's priority for scheduling but does not create a strict performance SLA. Redwood may throttle or preempt burst allocations to maintain platform stability." Full wording in doc link.

pricing-bot: Note: round-trip impact on revenue model: prepaid packs shift recognition. Recommend pilot sell as "consumable add-on" not as committed capacity.

toni: GTM: need a single SKU name. Propose 'Burst Pack' + tiers (Starter, Business, Scale). Also need a price-per-pack and renewal behavior.

cheng: eng gating: need two things before pilot: 1) API flag for entitlement apply/remove; 2) simulated throttling mode for QA so we can show customer behavior without risking prod.

maya: launch gates for pilot: operational playbook + billing testcases + one CSM-run pilot with a customer willing to share telemetry.

alex: action items: cheng build entitlement flag + sim mode (due Wed), pricing-bot to propose pack sizes/prices (due Tue), legal-bot to drop contract snippet into pilot T&Cs (due Tue), maya produce buyer kit (due Thu). I'll recruit pilot candidate.

toni: one more ask from field: add a one-click in-console 'apply burst now' button with confirmation and cost estimate. UX should show remaining pack balance.

cheng: feasible. We'll need a lightweight webhook for immediate entitlement application and a usage stream for balance decrement.

alex: ok team — aim to pick final pilot model by EOD Fri. If no objections, we'll go with hybrid baseline+burst-packs with concurrency-minute credits, 3x surge multiplier for on-demand top-ups, and best-effort contractual language.

maya: noted. I'll draft the pilot announcement and share tomorrow. Thanks all :rocket:
